title: SlipX actuator and electrical limits
description:
limits.yaml: what the car cannot exceed. Kept separate from dynamics.yaml because limits are a property of the hardware fitted, and swapping a servo or a battery changes this file and nothing else.

Several fields below are accepted and validated but not yet consumed: the ESC and servo models are CORE-08 and CORE-10 and arrive with L2 in P1. They are in the schema now so that a car directory written today is still valid then, and so that a team measuring their car has somewhere to put the numbers.

max_angle.description: Road wheel travel, symmetric, as a positive magnitude. [rad] Not a servo pulse width and not degrees. Consumed from L0.

max_rate.description: Servo slew rate limit. [rad/s] Consumed from L2 (CORE-10). Identifiable by commanding a step and timing the response.

bandwidth.description: Second-order servo natural frequency. [rad/s] Consumed from L2 (CORE-10).

damping.description: Second-order servo damping ratio. [-] Consumed from L2.

accel_max.description: Peak forward acceleration the drivetrain can deliver. [m/s^2] At L0 and L1 this is the whole drivetrain model; from L2 it is superseded by the ESC torque-speed curve and becomes a bound rather than the mechanism.

decel_max.description: Peak braking deceleration, as a positive magnitude. [m/s^2] Brake bias deliberately does not appear: a 1/10 car brakes through the motor, and a brake bias field would be a parameter nobody can set (CORE-08).

electrical.description: Consumed from L2 (CORE-08, CORE-09). Battery sag is what makes the last lap slower than the first, and a car tuned without it is tuned for a battery state that lasts thirty seconds.

pack_nominal_v.description: Nominal pack voltage. [V] 11.1 for a 3S lithium polymer.

pack_internal_resistance.description: Internal resistance, which is what produces sag under load. [ohm]

regen_current_max.description: Regenerative braking current limit, its own limit and usually well below current_max. [A]
